launch-tx-san-antonio-brackenridge-park.description: The free Japanese Tea Garden fills a former quarry with stone paths, ponds, bridges, waterfall, shaded plants, an overlook, accessible parking, and a cafe.
San Antonio Zoo is a separately ticketed attraction with its own gates, hours, security, restrooms, food, parking guidance, and animal-program schedule.
The miniature Zoo Eagle train boards near the zoo and makes a family loop through the park; tickets, queues, weather, and operating times are separate.
Three named walking routes follow portions of the San Antonio River through shade, historic structures, crossings, picnic areas, and attraction edges.
The historic open-air Sunken Garden Theater occupies a former quarry beside the Tea Garden and opens according to performances and rentals.
Lambert Beach is a historic former swimming area and current picnic and field zone; deteriorated river access is not an operating public beach.
Lions Field playground sits east of the main attraction core near neighborhood recreation facilities and its own parking approach.
The Witte is a separately ticketed museum campus on the park edge with science, nature, culture, family exhibits, food, restrooms, and its own schedule.

launch-tx-san-antonio-hemisfair.description: Yanaguana Garden is the inclusive family hub with climbing, swings, toddler play, sand, games, splash access, seating, restrooms, and nearby food.
The free seasonal splash pad operates 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. March-October unless weather, maintenance, or an event changes access.
Civic Park's Great Lawn is a large flexible green for picnics, play, fitness, festivals, and performances and may close for event setup or turf recovery.
The Springs are shallow constructed water features in Civic Park for cooling and gathering, distinct from the separately scheduled splash pad.
Tower Park's basketball court and recreation space sit within the broader district and can be affected by events or adjacent development.
Sand play provides open-ended digging near Yanaguana Garden; expect wet clothing, tracked sand, and close child supervision.
Public art and historic structures are distributed across Hemisfair, best explored on foot between Civic Park, Yanaguana Garden, and Tower Park.
Restaurants occupy restored historic houses and newer buildings around the parks; each has independent hours, prices, seating, and pet policies.

launch-tx-san-antonio-phil-hardberger-pa.description: The broad vegetated Tobin Land Bridge carries people and wildlife over Wurzbach Parkway and connects the east and west trail networks.
The elevated Skywalk winds through the tree canopy near the Land Bridge with gentle grades, overlooks, and occasional congestion.
The 1.8-acre east dog park has separate small- and all-dog areas and a distinctive two-story doghouse, open sunrise to sunset.
The 1.5-acre west dog park includes agility equipment and separate use areas near the NW Military Highway entrance.
The east playground and nature-play amenities are reached from Blanco Road and sit apart from the west-side facilities.
The west playground, Little Free Library, and picnic facilities are closest to the Urban Ecology Center entrance.
The Urban Ecology Center supports programs, exhibits, classrooms, gatherings, restrooms, and park orientation but is not an always-open heat shelter.
The Salado Creek Greenway connection extends the visit beyond Hardberger into a longer trail network; plan distance, water, and return routing.

launch-tx-san-antonio-san-antonio-river-.description: The downtown loop is the busiest 24-hour river-level section with restaurants, hotels, bridges, stairs, boat landings, crowds, and landmark access.
Museum Reach extends north through public art, locks, quieter paths, museums, and Pearl, and remains open 24 hours.
Mission Reach is a daylight-only naturalized trail corridor toward the historic missions with trailheads, habitat, art, flood risk, and fewer businesses.
Arneson River Theatre places a stage across the river from stepped seating and opens according to performances, rehearsals, and special events.
Rivercenter provides a major downtown river-level access point with shops, food, restrooms, garage parking, elevators, and private operating hours.
Pearl access connects Museum Reach with dining, market activity, Hotel Emma, public spaces, and heavy weekend pedestrian traffic.
Boat landings serve narrated cruises, shuttles, and private events; routes, queues, prices, accessibility, and schedules vary by operator.
Public art, the Grotto, bridges, and landscaped passages reward a slower Museum Reach walk; not every installation is visible from street level.

launch-tx-san-antonio-san-antonio-missio.description: Mission Concepcion is the northernmost park mission, known for unrestored stone architecture and original frescoes, with a contact station and accessible parking.
Mission San Jose is the largest mission and park orientation center, with visitor center, film, store, ranger walks, compound, church, gristmill, and restrooms.
Mission San Juan includes a church, farm fields, acequia, contact station, picnic area, restrooms, and access to the short nature trail.
Mission Espada is the southernmost mission, with a compact compound, museum/contact station, active church, acequia landscape, and nearby aqueduct.
The Mission Reach trail links downtown and the four missions for walking and biking over a long daylight-only river corridor with many trailheads.
The historic Espada Aqueduct is a fragile self-guided site with a small lot and benches but no restrooms, drinking water, or climbing access.
The Mission San Jose Visitor Center is the best first stop for maps, Junior Ranger books, orientation film, ranger guidance, accessible restrooms, and park store.
San Juan Nature Trail is a short sunrise-to-sunset route through river and mission landscape that can close for mud, flooding, heat, or habitat work.

launch-tx-san-antonio-san-pedro-springs-.description: The large historic outdoor pool is posted open 1:00-8:00 p.m. daily except Tuesday during the current 2026 season; staffing, weather, maintenance, and seasonal dates can still alter operation.
The springs and landscaped water preserve a 12,000-year gathering place but are not an unsupervised alternative to the public swimming pool.
The reservable gazebo sits in the historic landscape without built-in electricity, picnic tables, or lighting and has a four-hour reservation minimum.
The playground provides neighborhood play near shaded park paths, picnics, and civic facilities; check equipment heat despite mature trees.
The skate plaza offers unsupervised wheeled recreation with posted rules and shared access near other park users.
McFarlin Tennis Center is a separately managed sports facility with court schedules, fees, reservations, and event access.
San Pedro Playhouse is a separately ticketed theater on park grounds with its own performance schedule, entrance, parking, and restroom access.
San Pedro Library is a public branch beside the park with independent hours, indoor services, programs, and rules.

launch-tx-san-antonio-pearsall-park.description: The large free splash-pad zone operates 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. March-October and is separated from some of the park's other major activity areas.
The destination playground combines large structures, swings, terrain play, zip line, rubber surfacing, and nearby family amenities with limited natural shade.
San Antonio's largest city skate park contains bowls, transitions, rails, ledges, and open riding areas with no assumption of staff supervision.
The 1.5-acre dog park uses a combined large- and small-dog area rather than fully separated enclosures; leash dogs immediately outside it.
The free 18-hole, par-58 disc golf course stretches 5,680 feet through exposed terrain and requires visitors to bring their own discs.
Multiple 5K walking and running routes avoid street and park-road crossings, with heat, hills, distance, and water planning still essential.
The automated 40-yard sprint timer is part of a broader fitness challenge area with rings, pull-up bars, steps, and workout canopy.
Wickiup Overlook uses sculptural shade, limestone, granite, and elevated views toward Lackland, downtown, and the park's broad former-landfill landscape.

launch-tx-san-antonio-woodlawn-lake-park.description: The paved lake loop connects the playground, pool, dog park, gym, Island House, fitness stations, sports facilities, fishing, and neighborhood entrances.
The seasonal public pool at 221 Alexander Avenue has open-swim and weekday lap-swim schedules separate from the park's midnight closing time.
The playground provides family play near picnic and lake amenities; identify the nearest restroom and check surfaces for dangerous heat.
The designated dog park provides off-leash exercise within the larger lake park; leash dogs on the loop and near all other facilities.
The small lighthouse is Woodlawn Lake's signature visual landmark and a useful orientation point rather than an open climbing structure.
The Island House is a reservable event facility reached within the lake landscape and is not continuously open for casual indoor use.
The community gym and related rooms support sports, classes, programs, and reservations on facility-specific schedules.
Fishing is allowed from designated shoreline areas under Texas licensing rules; the lake is not open for swimming.
